sections.title: The toolkit you already have
sections.content: You already have everything you need to explain a problem: elromlik ("to break down"), nem működik ("it doesn't work"), eltűnik ("to disappear"), plus kellene, tud and lehet for asking someone to help. Put them together and you can handle almost anything that goes wrong.

items.spanish: Elnézést, elromlott a zuhany a szobámban, tudna segíteni?
items.english: Excuse me, the shower in my room broke, could you help?

items.spanish: Sajnos nem működik a wifi, pedig tegnap még jó volt.
items.english: Unfortunately the wifi isn't working, even though it was fine yesterday.

items.spanish: Eltűnt a kulcsom, ezért nem tudok bemenni a lakásba.
items.english: My key has disappeared, so I can't get into the flat.

sections.content: tudna is the polite conditional of tud — Tudna segíteni? ("Could you help?") sounds much softer than the plain present Tud segíteni?, the same way "could you" is softer than "can you" in English.
